Configuration.AuthFlowNote: API-key bearer over the Stripe SECRET key (sk_live_.../sk_test_...) -- a single, long-lived secret key, NOT OAuth2 (no authorization code flow, no client id/secret pair, no refresh token). Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <secret_key>`. A `Stripe-Version` header pins the API version the request is interpreted against (date-versioned, e.g. `2026-06-24.dahlia`) -- omitting it defaults to the key's account-pinned version. Confirmed from the OpenAPI spec's global security scheme (HTTP bearer) plus docs.stripe.com/api overview text.

AuthAdditionalHeaders.Stripe-Version: <API version string, e.g. 2026-06-24.dahlia> -- pins the response shape; omit to use the key's account-default pinned version
AuthAdditionalHeaders.Idempotency-Key: <client-generated key, POST only> -- required for safe retry of Create operations; 24h server-side cache; Stripe validates parameter consistency on replay with the same key

Configuration.CredentialShape: single secret key (sk_live_... for production, sk_test_... for Stripe's self-serve test mode -- a real API surface, not a mock)
Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: Secret keys are long-lived and do not expire; there is no OAuth2 token/refresh-token pair to rotate in the standard API-key integration model (Stripe Connect's OAuth flow for platform/connected-account authorization is a distinct, out-of-scope-for-this-slot mechanism from the direct secret-key auth this connector uses).

universalPK.note: Every in-scope top-level resource schema declares a required, non-expandable `id: string` property (description: "Unique identifier for the object.") plus a companion `object` discriminator enum naming the resource type. Confirmed identically across all 33 in-scope OpenAPI component schemas (spec3.json/spec3.sdk.json). Human-readable ID prefixes (cus_, ch_, pi_, in_, sub_, acct_, etc.) are well-known informally but Stripe explicitly disclaims them as a guaranteed/contractual list (docs: adding/removing a fixed prefix is considered backwards-compatible) -- so `id` (opaque string, <=255 chars) is the only structurally-guaranteed PK contract; prefixes are NOT encoded as a hard constraint.

PaginationDefaults.cursorParamNote: starting_after and ending_before are mutually exclusive -- starting_after pages forward (older records), ending_before pages backward (newer records) through the reverse-chronological list. The cursor value is the `id` of the last object in the current page's `data[]` array.
PaginationDefaults.note: Confirmed 3 independent ways (SOURCE_STUDY.md S3): (1) byte-identical prose in every list endpoint's `limit` parameter description across all 30 checked list-capable objects ("Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10") -- Stripe encodes this bound in description PROSE, not JSON Schema maximum/default, so a connector extractor must read the text, not schema constraints; (2) docs.stripe.com/api/pagination confirms the {object:'list', data:[], has_more, url} envelope and starting_after/ending_before semantics; (3) stripe-node's autoPagination.ts implements exactly has_more/starting_after/ending_before with lastId cursor tracking. `source` and `token` objects have NO list endpoint at all (create+get-by-id only, by deliberate Stripe security design) -- PaginationType is inapplicable for those two IOs specifically.

IncrementalSyncCapability.coverage: 24 of 30 direct list-capable objects document the `created` range filter (confirmed present in the OpenAPI spec's per-endpoint parameter list); absent on payment_method, subscription_item, quote, payment_link (which genuinely lack a created filter in the spec) and on source/token (which have no list endpoint at all). SupportsIncrementalSync + IncrementalWatermarkField='created' are emitted ONLY on the 24 objects where the spec proves the filter; left undefined on the other 6 -- provable-only, never assumed universal.
IncrementalSyncCapability.eventsAPIAlternative: The Events API (/v1/events, filterable by `type` and `created`) provides a change-notification stream across nearly all mutable objects and can serve as a supplementary/alternative incremental mechanism, but per-object list-endpoint range filtering is the primary documented incremental path modeled here.

Configuration.WebhooksNote: Stripe delivers webhook events for the `event` object (thin-events design: 150+ named event.type values, e.g. charge.succeeded, customer.subscription.updated, invoice.paid) to endpoints configured via the (out-of-scope, separately-enrolled) Webhook Endpoints management API. Payloads are signed.
Configuration.WebhooksSignatureNote: The Stripe-Signature header carries a timestamp + one or more v1 HMAC-SHA256 signatures computed over `<timestamp>.<raw_request_body>` using the endpoint's signing secret; confirmed from docs.stripe.com webhook-signature-verification convention (well-documented, standard Stripe pattern -- referenced here as the vendor's stated mechanism, not independently re-derived in this credential-free build).
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: Stripe has NO general-purpose batch/bulk write endpoint for the in-scope core resources (confirmed: every Create/Update/Delete operation in the OpenAPI spec is single-resource). Writes are single-resource POSTs; no batch create/update/delete path exists to encode. (Distinct from Stripe's separate, out-of-scope bulk-data products such as Sigma/Reporting.)
Configuration.APIVersioningNote: Stripe pins the API version via the `Stripe-Version` request header (date-based version string, e.g. `2026-06-24.dahlia`), NOT via a URL path segment (the path is always /v1/...) and NOT via an Accept-header media-type parameter. A key has an account-default pinned version used when the header is omitted. Confirmed from the OpenAPI spec's info.version field + docs.stripe.com/api overview (API versioning section).
Configuration.WriteBodyEncodingNote: BINDING IDIOSYNCRASY (SOURCE_STUDY.md S4.1): every one of the 292 POST/PUT/PATCH requestBody definitions in the OpenAPI spec declares `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` content -- ZERO json request bodies anywhere in the API (the sole exception is POST /v1/files, `multipart/form-data`, for binary file upload -- itself an out-of-scope object). Nested/array attributes use bracket notation (e.g. `address[line1]=123+Main+St`, `metadata[key]=value`, `items[0][price]=price_123`). All GET responses ARE standard JSON. A connector that POSTs JSON bodies against this API will not work -- the write-path HTTP layer MUST serialize as form-urlencoded with bracket notation, never JSON.stringify.
Configuration.UpdateVerbConventionNote: Stripe uses POST (never PATCH or PUT) for Update operations on every in-scope resource -- confirmed via per-operation path method presence across all 33 in-scope schemas (SOURCE_STUDY.md S2.1 table). The distinguishing factor between Create and Update is the PATH (collection root vs. /{id}), not the HTTP verb -- both are POST.
Configuration.DeleteResponseShapeNote: DELETE operations (where supported -- not universal; many resources use a soft-delete-by-active:false pattern instead, e.g. product/price/plan/coupon) respond HTTP 200 with a `deleted_<object>` tombstone body shape: `{deleted: true, id: '<the deleted id>', object: '<object type>'}` (confirmed via components.schemas.deleted_customer etc., required:[deleted,id,object]). DeleteIDLocation=body, read the `id` field of the tombstone response, NOT a Location header and NOT a 204-with-no-body pattern.

ErrorResponseShape.envelope: { error: { type, code, message, param, doc_url, ... } }
ErrorResponseShape.envelopeSource: components.schemas.api_errors -- confirmed present on every error response across the spec.

ErrorResponseShape.rateLimitHeaderNote: Present on 429 responses; identifies WHICH limit was breached, feeding the connector's ExtractRetryAfterMs / backoff-target logic.

RateLimitPolicy.note: Confirmed ExplicitStatement from docs.stripe.com/rate-limits (SourceTier 1, OfficialDocs). BatchMaxRequestCount=100 / BatchRequestWaitTime=1 (seconds) encode the LIVE-mode steady-state ceiling; test-mode keys (used in this credential-free build's eventual live-read path) are throttled to 25 req/s -- the connector's rate limiter should apply the tighter test-mode figure when a sk_test_ key is detected, or default conservatively when mode is unknown.

perResourceOverrides.paymentIntentsUpdate: 1000 updates per Payment Intent per hour
perResourceOverrides.subscriptionsNewInvoices: 10 new invoices per subscription per minute, 20 per day

RateLimitPolicy.perResourceOverridesNote: Documented per-resource exceptions to the account-wide 100/25 req/s baseline (docs.stripe.com/rate-limits, ExplicitStatement). Not all are directly relevant to the in-scope object set (Files API is out of scope) but are recorded for connector-side throttle tuning where applicable (payment_intent, subscription, payout are in-scope).

IdempotencySupport.note: Confirmed ExplicitStatement from docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests. Stripe validates parameter consistency on replay with the same key (a replay with the SAME key but DIFFERENT parameters returns an error, not a silent overwrite). The connector's Create path should generate and send a deterministic Idempotency-Key per logical create attempt to make retries safe.

Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternNote: Stripe does not support customer-defined custom OBJECTS (no equivalent to HubSpot's p_<accountID>_<name> custom-object convention) -- the object catalog is fixed by Stripe's own API surface. Every in-scope resource DOES expose a generic `metadata: Hash` field (arbitrary string key-value pairs, up to 50 keys, key<=40 chars, value<=500 chars) as the sanctioned custom-DATA extension point. CustomObjectMarkerPattern is left null (no such concept exists on this vendor); CustomFieldMarkerPattern names the generic `metadata` field as where customer-defined key/value data lives (not a naming PATTERN on a canonical field name, since there is only the one universal field).
Configuration.WriteCapabilityNote: Per-object operation map derived directly from the OpenAPI spec's per-path method presence (SOURCE_STUDY.md S2.1 table) -- POST-create, POST-update (Stripe uses POST for both verbs), DELETE where the spec declares it. Many resources are deliberately non-deletable via hard DELETE (charge, payment_intent, setup_intent, payment_method, refund, dispute, balance_transaction, event, price, invoiceitem's sibling credit_note, promotion_code, tax_rate, quote, transfer, application_fee, topup, checkout.session, payment_link, capability) -- Stripe's documented alternative for several of these (product/price/plan/coupon aside, which DO support hard delete) is a soft-deactivate pattern (e.g. `active:false`) rather than DELETE; capability<->method bijection is honored per-IO in the IntegrationObject rows (Delete columns null where the spec has no DELETE operation). This connector is HEAVILY write-capable overall (create+update+delete on the large majority of resources) -- deliberately NOT pull-only.
Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: No ETag, no If-Match/If-Unmodified-Since precondition header, and no explicit optimistic-concurrency version field documented anywhere in the OpenAPI spec's request/response shapes for the in-scope objects. Stripe's own consistency model for concurrent writes is last-write-wins at the field level (each POST update only touches the parameters supplied) rather than a client-supplied version token. Conflict handling for bidirectional sync (if ever enabled) must rely on snapshot 3-way merge, NOT a real ETag/version-based MostRecent resolution -- there is no vendor-side signal to support the latter.
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNote: Genuinely mixed by object, not a single vendor-wide answer (provable-only -- do not collapse to one value). HARD delete (real DELETE verb, 200 + deleted_<object> tombstone body, SOURCE_STUDY.md S4.2) is documented for: customer, product, plan, subscription, subscription_item, invoice, invoiceitem, coupon, account, person. SOFT/deactivate delete (no DELETE verb; the vendor's documented alternative is setting `active:false` on product/price/plan/coupon-family resources) applies to price (no DELETE at all; deactivate via update `active:false`) and is the vendor-recommended alternative even on the resources that DO also support hard delete (product/plan/coupon). All OTHER in-scope resources (charge, payment_intent, refund, dispute, balance_transaction, payout, event, invoiceitem-adjacent credit_note, promotion_code, tax_rate, quote, transfer, application_fee, topup, checkout.session, payment_link, source, token, external_account, capability) have NO delete operation of any kind documented -- 'none'. Per-EntityMap DeleteBehavior should default per-object from this map, never a single blanket vendor default.
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Read-only Pull is the recommended default for EVERY object per the read-first discipline, regardless of Stripe's extensive write capability. Stripe is a live financial system of record (real charges, real money movement) -- pushing/creating/updating/deleting here has direct monetary and customer-facing consequences. Bidirectional sync must be explicitly opted into per-object AFTER sandbox validation (Stripe's self-serve sk_test_ test-mode key is the correct place to validate write behavior before any live/production enablement) -- never defaulted on.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNote: IF bidirectional sync is later enabled for a given object, DestWins/SourceWins/MostRecent are all unsafe defaults here: MostRecent requires a reliable last-modified timestamp+ETag/version signal for conflict arbitration, and ConcurrencyControl='none' means Stripe supplies no such signal (Stripe objects do carry per-field mutation but no document-level version/ETag to compare). DestWins/SourceWins risk silently overwriting real financial state (e.g. a locally-edited subscription vs. a webhook-driven remote change) without human awareness. Manual conflict resolution is the only policy consistent with the absence of a concurrency-control primitive AND the financial stakes of this vendor's data -- surface conflicts for human review rather than auto-resolving.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Card-issuing program surface (cards, authorizations, disputes) -- a distinct, separately-enrollable Stripe product most payments/billing data-sync consumers do not ingest.
Embedded-banking money-movement ledger -- separate product requiring Treasury enrollment.
In-person POS hardware/readers management.
Automated tax calculation/filing product, distinct from the in-scope tax_rate object.
Modern usage-based billing (the usage_record successor) -- a distinct metering subsystem, itself out of the requested 34-object core.
Bank-account-linking/read product (Plaid-like), separately enrollable.
Pre-built embeddable UI configuration objects for Connect platforms -- config schemas, not syncable data records.
Fraud-detection rules/review engine.
Carbon-removal purchase product.
ID-verification product (the gelato_* internal schemas).
SaaS feature-gating product.
Scheduled report-run generation.
Self-serve customer subscription-management portal configuration.
Sandbox-only simulation endpoints (test clocks etc.) -- never present in live mode.
SQL-based analytics query product.
Binary/document upload storage, not a payments/billing data record.
Stripe Apps marketplace secret-storage.
Webhook subscription configuration management, distinct from the in-scope event object itself.

Connect platform reserve-fund holds (reserve.hold/plan/release + reserve_transaction) and platform-internal shapes (application, connect_collection_transfer). No list/get paths in the spec — these are embedded/internal Connect ledger sub-shapes, not independently-syncable records most payments/billing consumers ingest.

POST-only, short-lived session/link/ephemeral-key/funding-instruction objects. No GET-list surface and no id-addressable record to re-read — they are one-shot client-secret/URL mints (the NON_SYNCABLE class), not durable records to sync.

source_mandate_notification is a legacy Sources-API mandate-notification sub-shape; tax_deducted_at_source is a deprecated India-specific tax-withholding shape. No list/get paths; not part of the core payments/billing/connect/checkout surface.
Card-data request-forwarding product (forward a raw card request to a third-party endpoint) — a distinct, separately-used Stripe feature outside the core payments/billing sync surface.

Configuration.OutOfScopeObjectFamiliesNote: 22 named families covering 464 of 1703 enumerated OpenAPI schemas. Each spec-provable (schema/path counts derived from spec3.sdk.json). Amendment round 2 added the residual advisory objects: the genuine in-scope borderline candidates (country_spec, exchange_rate, review, tax_code, apple_pay_domain, payment_method_configuration, payment_method_domain, product_feature, discount) were PROMOTED to full IOs; the specialized-product-line and non-syncable session/link/ephemeral objects were recorded here. Narrowing remains a deliberate, evidenced scope decision (payments+billing+connect+checkout core), never a silent cap.

If the first invoice is not paid within 23 hours, the subscription transitions to `incomplete_expired`. This is a terminal status, the open invoice will be voided and no further invoices will be generated. A subscription that is currently in a trial period is `trialing` and moves to `active` when the trial period is over. A subscription can only enter a `paused` status [when a trial ends without a payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/trials#create-free-trials-without-payment). A `paused` subscription doesn't generate invoices and can be resumed after your customer adds their payment method. The `paused` status is different from [pausing collection](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/pause-payment), which still generates invoices and leaves the subscription's status unchanged. If subscription `collection_method=charge_automatically`, it becomes `past_due` when payment is required but cannot be paid (due to failed payment or awaiting additional user actions). Once Stripe has exhausted all payment retry attempts, the subscription will become `canceled` or `unpaid` (depending on your subscriptions settings). If subscription `collection_method=send_invoice` it becomes `past_due` when its invoice is not paid by the due date, and `canceled` or `unpaid` if it is still not paid by an additional deadline after that. Note that when a subscription has a status of `unpaid`, no subsequent invoices will be attempted (invoices will be created, but then immediately automatically closed).
